thread.title: Thai Stock Market May Extend Winning Streak

author: rttnews.com
title: Thai Stock Market May Extend Winning Streak
text:
Thai Stock Market May Extend Winning Streak 9/27/2018 10:30 PM ET
The Thai stock market has ticked higher in two straight sessions, gathering almost 5 points or 0.3 percent along the way. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now rests just above the 1,750-point plateau and it's expected to see additional support on Friday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is firm, with support expected from the oil and technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were up and the Asian bourses are tipped to follow suit.
The SET finished slightly higher on Thursday as gains from the financial shares were offset by weakness from the cement stocks and a mixed picture from the energy producers.
For the day, the index picked up 3.02 points or 0.17 percent to finish at 1,752.95 after trading between 1,735.58 and 1,753.16. Volume was 14.091 billion shares worth 63.424 billion baht. There were 698 decliners and 610 gainers, with 581 stocks finishing unchanged.
Among the actives, Thailand Airport added 0.38 percent, while Banpu skidded 1.03 percent, Bangkok Bank and Kasikornbank both collected 0.47 percent, Beauty Community jumped 1.69 percent, Bangkok Expressway shed 0.57 percent, Krung Thai Bank perked 1.01 percent, PTT lost 0.46 percent, PTT Exploration and Production advanced 0.97 percent, Siam Commercial Bank surged 2.42 percent, Siam Concrete slid 0.44 percent and PTT Global Chemical, Charoen Pokphand Foods, Advanced Info and Bangkok Medical were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is upbeat as stocks opened higher on Thursday. They faded slightly in the afternoon but still finished firmly in the green.
The Dow added 54.65 points or 0.21 percent to 26,439.93, while the NASDAQ gained 51.60 points or 0.65 percent to 8,041.97 and the S&P was up 8.03 points or 0.28 percent to 2,914.00.
A notable advance by shares of Apple (AAPL) contributed to the higher close on Wall Street after J.P. Morgan initiated coverage of the company's stock with an Overweight rating.
In economic news, the Commerce Department noted a bigger than expected jump in durable goods orders in August. The Commerce Department also said the pace of U.S. economic growth in the second quarter was unrevised at 4.2 percent from the previous estimate.
Also, the Labor Department noted a rebound in initial jobless claims in the week ended September 22. And the National Association of Realtors said pending home sales dropped much more than expected in August.
Crude oil prices moved higher on Thursday, amid concerns that sanctions on Iran from November may result in supply shortage in the market. Crude oil futures for November delivery ended up $0.55 or 0.8 percent at $72.12 a barrel.
Closer to home, Thailand will release August data for imports, exports and trade balance later today. In July, imports were worth $19.44 billion and exports were at $20.30 billion for a trade surplus of $0.86 billion.
